Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Horizon Capital Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, participants are required to utilize the conference ID number followed by the pound key for any technical difficulties. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Capital Partners' Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Mitchell, Chief Financial Officer; David Kwon, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Chen, Head of Distribution; Michael Torres, Head of Operations; and Elena Vasquez, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by the impact of market performance and net flows on our assets under management. Our AUM grew to $1.25 trillion.

To recap the dynamics, average daily AUM for the quarter stood at $1.22 trillion, reflecting a $65 billion increase driven by two primary levers—market performance, which contributed approximately $42 billion or 65% of the growth, and net client inflows of $23 billion, accounting for the remaining 35%. This marks our 11th straight quarter of positive organic flows, underscoring the durability of our multi-asset class platform amid a volatile macro backdrop.

Market performance was the dominant tailwind this quarter. Global equities rallied sharply, with the MSCI World Index up 9.2% and the S&P 500 delivering a robust 10.8% return, fueled by resilient U.S. corporate earnings, AI-driven tech sector gains—think Nvidia and the Magnificent Seven—and cooling inflation data that bolstered rate cut expectations. Our equity strategies, which represent 42% of total AUM or $525 billion, benefited disproportionately, adding $28 billion in appreciation alone. Active large-cap growth funds, like our Horizon Growth Equity Fund mirroring the Russell 1000 Growth, saw 11.5% returns net of fees, outpacing the benchmark by 120 basis points.

Fixed income, at 28% of AUM or $350 billion, contributed $9 billion, though performance was more muted at +3.1% amid a 25 bps Fed funds cut and a flattening yield curve. Our core-plus strategies, including EMU investment-grade sleeves benchmarked to Bloomberg Euro Aggregate, navigated duration extension effectively, with our active bond platform delivering 4.2%—ahead of peers. Alternatives, now 18% of AUM at $225 billion, added $4 billion, driven by private credit yields compressing to SOFR +450 bps and a rebound in real assets like infrastructure amid energy transition tailwinds.

Regionally, North America drove 70% of market gains, with U.S.-centric ETFs like our HCP S&P 500 UCITS ETF gathering steam. EMEA saw mixed results—European equities up 7% on ECB dovishness, but UK gilts underperformed amid fiscal concerns. APAC was the outlier, flat at +1.2% due to China property sector woes, though our Japan equity sleeves, tied to TOPIX, surged 12% on BOJ normalization.

Shifting to net flows, our $23 billion of organic inflows represent a 15% acceleration from Q2's $20 billion and beat our internal target by 20%. This was broad-based but skewed toward lower-fee products, with ETFs and model portfolios capturing 55% or $12.6 billion. Retail channels via platforms like Schwab and Vanguard's ecosystem drove $9 billion, fueled by our suite of low-cost beta products—our Core Equity ETF suite alone saw $4.2 billion in inflows, with expense ratios averaging 8 bps. Institutional flows hit $8 billion, led by defined contribution plans and wirehouse SMAs, where our separately managed accounts grew 18% YoY to $180 billion, benefiting from customization in ESG overlays.

Product-wise, passive strategies outperformed active this quarter, with $15 billion into ETFs versus $5 billion into active mutual funds—a 25% mix shift reflecting investor preference for cost efficiency amid beta outperformance. However, our alpha-generating active equities bucked the trend with $3.5 billion, particularly in small-cap value funds capitalizing on the Russell 2000's 8% rebound. On the outflow front, we saw modest $2.5 billion redemptions from legacy high-duration bond funds, but these were more than offset by reallocations into our short-duration TIPS and floating-rate notes, which align with our 'barbell' fixed income positioning.

Sarah Mitchell: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Horizon Capital Partners delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $5.65 billion, representing an 18% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by the impact of AUM changes on our revenue.

As you know, we manage $1.25 trillion in assets under management as of quarter-end, spanning a diversified suite of public market strategies—including our flagship Horizon Equity ETF suite, fixed income SMAs, and multi-asset solutions—as well as growing alternatives like private credit and infrastructure funds.

Our revenue formula is straightforward: Revenue equals Average AUM times Blended Fee Rate, with modest contributions from performance fees, which added $150 million this quarter from our hedge fund composites outperforming benchmarks like the HFRI Fund Weighted Composite by 250 bps.

Ending AUM grew 10.1% quarter-over-quarter to $1.25 trillion, outpacing the industry average of 7-8% as reported by peers like BlackRock and State Street. This growth decomposed into three key components: market appreciation/depreciation of +7.8% impact, or +$92 billion—equities were the standout, with our $650 billion equity franchise benefiting from the S&P 500's 7.2% rally, fueled by AI-themed tech names like NVIDIA and broader rotation into value cyclicals. Our active equity strategies captured 110% of the benchmark return, thanks to overweight positions in semiconductors and renewables. Fixed income AUM, at $350 billion, added +2.1% from a flattening yield curve—our core-plus bond funds gained 1.8% amid Fed signals of just two more rate cuts in 2024. Alternatives like our $150 billion private markets book saw muted +0.5% gains due to valuation lags in illiquid infrastructure deals.

Organic net flows: +2.3% impact, or +$28 billion—net inflows accelerated to $28 billion—the strongest quarter since Q4 2022—driven by institutional mandates and retail momentum. Long-term flows were positive across regions: U.S. clients contributed $12 billion into our low-cost Core ETFs (now at 12 bps average fee, competing head-on with Vanguard's VTI), Europe added $9 billion in ESG fixed income amid MiFID II-driven sustainability mandates, and APAC delivered $7 billion, particularly in our China A-shares strategies amid post-COVID reopening tailwinds. Short-term money market flows were flat at +$1 billion, as yields on our $100 billion prime funds held above 5.25%. Notably, we saw $3 billion in outflows from underperforming small-cap active funds, but these were more than offset by wins in our quant-enhanced multi-asset platform, which now represents 15% of AUM.

FX and other: +0.0% impact—neutral overall, as the strengthening USD headwind (-1.2% on our $250 billion non-USD AUM) was balanced by hedging overlays in our global mandates. European and emerging market exposures, benchmarked against MSCI EAFE and EM indices, were protected via FX forwards, limiting drag to under 20 bps.

Translating AUM to revenue impact: This AUM mix-shift directly flowed through to revenue at our 48 bps blended rate. Q2 Average AUM: $1.08 trillion to Q3: $1.18 trillion (+9.2%). Fee Revenue uplift: ~$520 million from AUM growth alone. Fee rate stability preserved another $100 million versus expectations of 1-2 bps compression. Performance fees from our 2-and-20 alternatives pods—e.g., our direct lending fund returning 12% annualized—added upside. Regionally, Americas revenue grew 14% (65% of total), EMEA 10% (amid UCITS ETF launches), and APAC 22% (highest margin at 55 bps, driven by higher-beta EM equities).

Our expenses were $4.2 billion, resulting in net income of $1.1 billion. Our expense ratio improved due to ongoing investments in scalable technology platforms that have optimized our cost base while supporting higher AUM volumes.

We're not immune to macro pressures. Fee compression persists—our passive ETF fees dipped to 11 bps from 13 bps YoY—as clients flock to zero-fee indexers like Fidelity's ZERO funds. Equity beta exposure amplified market volatility; a 5% S&P drawdown could shave 3-4% off AUM quarterly. Yet, we're ahead of the curve: our AUM mix has shifted 5% toward higher-margin alternatives (now 12% of total, targeting 20% by 2026).

Technical initiatives driving resilience: Our proprietary Aladdin-like portfolio management system processed 2.5 million trades daily, enabling sub-10 bps execution costs and unlocking $2 billion in new SMA flows from wirehouses like Morgan Stanley. We launched three new active ETFs—AI Growth, ESG Credit, and Buffered Outcome—aggregating $8 billion in Q2 inflows, with TERs at 25-35 bps. Enhanced our digital advisor arm to $50 billion AUM, boosting organic growth 30% QoQ via personalized model portfolios tied to risk premia factors.

Looking forward, we guide to 8-10% AUM growth in H2, assuming S&P +5-7% and net flows of $20-25 billion quarterly.

David Kwon: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by capitalizing on the drivers of net flows, such as fund performance and market trends.

For the third quarter, we posted net inflows of $18.7 billion, bringing our year-to-date total to $42.3 billion—a 28% increase over the same period last year. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of positive net flows across all major channels, underscoring the resilience of our franchise amid a volatile macro environment.

Our total AUM now stands at $1.47 trillion, up 12% quarter-over-quarter, with organic flows contributing 85% of that growth. Retail flows accounted for 62% or $11.6 billion, institutional flows 28% or $5.2 billion, and the remainder from high-net-worth individuals via our wealth management platforms.

Fund performance remains the single largest driver, responsible for approximately 45% of our Q3 net flows. Our active equity strategies, particularly the Horizon Alpha Equity Fund and our suite of sector-specific funds, continue to deliver compelling alpha. For instance, the Alpha Equity Fund generated a 1.2% three-year annualized alpha net of fees versus the S&P 500 benchmark, ranking in the top decile of the Morningstar Large-Cap Growth category. This performance resonance has driven $4.8 billion in inflows to our core equity platform, with retail investors reallocating from passive index funds amid the ongoing AI and tech rally.

In fixed income, our multi-sector bond strategies shone through. The Horizon Total Return Bond Fund returned 2.8% in Q3, outperforming its Bloomberg Aggregate benchmark by 110 basis points, fueled by our tactical overweight in investment-grade corporates and agency MBS. This attracted $3.2 billion in flows, as yield-hungry investors sought our 4.9% yield-to-worst amid falling rate expectations. Alternatives also contributed $2.1 billion, led by our evergreen private credit fund, which delivered a 12% net IRR over the past 12 months—well above peers—drawing institutional LP commitments from pension funds wary of public market volatility.

Performance attribution here is clear: our 150+ PMs and quant teams, leveraging our proprietary Horizon Insight AI platform, have enhanced stock selection and risk management. We've seen a 15% uptick in flows from advisors on platforms like Envestnet and Morningstar, where our funds' Sharpe ratios average 1.4 across the board.

Market dynamics amplified these performance-driven flows, contributing another 30% to our net flow momentum. The S&P 500's 15% YTD gain, propelled by the Magnificent Seven and broader small-cap rotation, created a favorable backdrop for our equity ETFs. Our Equity ETF suite saw $6.5 billion in inflows, with the Tech Innovators ETF alone capturing 22% market share in its category, with lower expense ratios at 12 bps.

Fixed income trends were equally supportive. With the 10-year Treasury yield dipping to 4.2% on Fed cut signals, we experienced a $4.1 billion rotation into short-duration and TIPS strategies. Our Ultra-Short Income ETF, yielding 5.1%, benefited from money market fund outflows as investors chased yield without duration risk.

ESG and thematic trends added $2.9 billion, with our Climate Transition Equity Fund inflows surging 40% QoQ amid EU SFDR regulations and U.S. SEC climate disclosure rules. Broader deglobalization themes boosted our infrastructure and defense-focused alternatives.

Conversely, we saw modest outflows of $1.1 billion from emerging markets equities due to China slowdown fears, but this was more than offset by our pivot to India and LatAm.

Beyond performance and markets, our proactive initiatives drove the remaining 25% of flows. Digitally, our revamped Advisor Portal—integrated with AI-driven portfolio construction tools—boosted retail advisor retention by 18%, generating $3.7 billion in recurring flows. We've onboarded 2,500 new RIAs YTD, leveraging APIs for seamless model delivery.

Product innovation was key: the launch of our Active ETF suite, including a 60/40 target-date ETF with dynamic glide paths, pulled in $2.4 billion on day-one demand.

Regionally, U.S. flows dominated at 68% or $12.7 billion, EMEA 18% or $3.4 billion, APAC 12% or $2.2 billion—up 55% YoY—and LatAm added $0.4 billion.

We launched our new AI Growth ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $500 million in AUM already and strong demand from institutional allocators seeking exposure to semiconductors and renewables.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in North America and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by net flows by channel: institutional, retail, alternatives.

For the quarter, we recorded net inflows of $15.2 billion across our channels, bringing year-to-date net flows to $48.7 billion. This marks our strongest quarterly flows since Q4 2021, driven by a favorable macro backdrop—including the Fed's recent 50bps rate cut and resilient equity markets—and our proactive product innovation.

Excluding money market funds, which saw $2.1 billion in seasonal outflows amid higher short-term yields, core long-term net flows were $17.3 billion, up 28% quarter-over-quarter. AUM ended the quarter at $1.47 trillion, reflecting 4.2% organic growth and market appreciation tailwinds from the S&P 500's 5.8% gain.

Institutional channel: $10.4 billion in net inflows (68% of total). Institutional remains our growth engine, with Q3 inflows accelerating 35% from Q2. This channel now represents 52% of our total AUM, up from 49% a year ago.

Key drivers included liability-driven investing (LDI) mandates, where we captured $4.2 billion, benefiting from UK gilt market stabilization and U.S. corporate pension de-risking. Our active fixed income strategies, particularly our Enhanced Core Bond Fund, saw $2.8 billion in wins, as clients rotated from cash amid yield curve steepening.

Regionally, North America contributed 62% of inflows ($6.5 billion), led by public plans reallocating to infrastructure debt. Europe rebounded with $2.9 billion (up 50% QoQ), fueled by Dutch and Nordic pensions favoring our UCITS-compliant multi-asset credit platform. APAC added $1.0 billion, primarily from sovereign wealth fund commitments to our private credit sleeve.

We're leaning into model portfolio delivery via APIs, integrating with BlackRock's Aladdin and State Street's Alpha platforms to win OCIO mandates. We closed two new $500 million+ OCIO relationships with U.S. endowments.

Retail channel: $4.3 billion in net inflows (28% of total), a 22% QoQ increase, though tempered by mutual fund outflows of $1.1 billion as investors favored lower-cost ETFs. This channel accounts for 38% of AUM.

ETFs drove 72% of inflows ($3.1 billion), led by our Core Equity ETF suite, which gathered $1.7 billion amid the 'Magnificent Seven' rally and small-cap rotation. Our active ETF launches—including the Global Thematic Growth ETF targeting AI and renewables—hit $850 million in first-quarter assets.

Mutual funds saw modest redemptions in equity ex-growth, but our target-date funds for DC plans bucked the trend with $900 million.

Regionally, U.S. wealth platforms like Schwab and Fidelity generated $2.6 billion (60%), EMEA retail added $1.2 billion via our partnership with Hargreaves Lansdown, and Asia ex-Japan contributed $500 million.

Our AI-driven personalization on our advisor portal improved conversion rates by 18% and reduced churn in SMAs.

Alternatives channel: $500 million in net inflows (4% of total, but accelerating), with AUM now at $185 billion (13% of total). Private equity led with $250 million into our evergreen PE fund targeting mid-market buyouts. Private credit drew $150 million from family offices seeking 10-12% yields. Real assets added $100 million.

Regionally, U.S. and Canada dominated at 55% ($275 million), Europe 30%, APAC 15%.

We're scaling our GP stakes platform, acquiring minority interests in niche managers, and launched a $1 billion evergreen alts ETF wrapper to democratize access.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 net flows of $16-20 billion.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on management fee revenue and average fee rate trends, as well as client retention rates and new client acquisition.

Management fee revenue came in at $478 million, up 11% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 10th consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY growth. On an annualized basis, this translates to a trailing 12-month management fee revenue of $1.92 billion.

Ending AUM reached $1.35 trillion, a robust 16% increase YoY and 5% sequentially, driven by strong organic net inflows of $28 billion and market appreciation of approximately 8%.

Average fee rates came in at 45.2 basis points for the quarter, down 30 bps YoY from 48.2 bps but stable sequentially. This moderation reflects the structural shift toward scale-oriented, lower-fee products.

Product mix evolution: Our ETF suite now represents 22% of total AUM, up from 15% a year ago. Long-term ETF net flows hit $12 billion. Higher-margin active equity strategies held steady at 32% of AUM, with fee rates averaging 72 bps.

Institutional AUM grew to 58% of the total, with average fees of 38 bps versus 55 bps in retail channels. Retail saw some pressure from wrap-fee programs.

Regionally, North America (72% of AUM): Fees held at 46 bps; EMEA (18%): expanded to 49 bps on 22% YoY AUM growth; APAC (10%): 52 bps amid $4 billion in inflows.

We're addressing fee headwinds through technology-led personalization: Our platform now serves 15% of institutional AUM, delivering 20-30 bps of embedded value through tax-loss harvesting—lifting blended fees by 5-10 bps net of compression. Scale in passives: on track to hit $300 billion in ETFs. Value-add overlays: ESG and alternatives now 25% of AUM at 65 bps.

We expect Q3 management fees to grow 9-12% YoY, with average fee rates stabilizing at 44-46 bps.

Turning to client dynamics, specifically client retention rates and new client acquisition, which remain the bedrock of our organic growth strategy. We're proud to report a trailing 12-month retention rate of 96.2%, up 220 basis points year-over-year and marking our 11th consecutive quarter above 95%. This is exceptional by industry standards—peers have hovered around 92-94%.

Retention calculated on a dollar-weighted basis: Institutional clients (65% of AUM): 97.8%; HNWIs and family offices (35%): 93.5%—an all-time high.

Regionally: North America (50% of clients): 96.5%; Europe (25%): 95.8%; APAC (15%): 97.2%; Emerging markets (10%): 94.1%.

Powering this: alpha generation—our Global Equity Composite outperformed the MSCI World by 320 bps net; client-centric tech—our AI-driven client portal has 85% uptake among HNWIs, reducing churn by 15%; relationship rigor—quarterly business reviews with NPS averaging 78.

New client acquisition: we delivered $28.4 billion in net new assets (NNA) over the quarter—up 18% QoQ and 22% YoY—representing a healthy 9.4% organic AUM growth rate. Gross inflows hit $35.2 billion, with outflows at $6.8 billion.

Sources: Institutional wins: $14.7 billion; Wealth channel: $9.1 billion; Alternatives and retail: $4.6 billion.

Regionally: APAC led with $8.9 billion (31%); Europe: $7.2 billion; North America: $10.1 billion; Rest of world: $2.2 billion.

Initiatives: product innovation—launching Alternatives Hub targeting $10 billion; distribution expansion—fintech tie-ups and RIA custody JV; ESG and thematic alpha—42% of new flows into sustainable funds.

We guide to $25-30 billion NNA in Q4, with retention above 96%.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and liquidity risks and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities, including through advanced stress testing and scenario analysis integrated into our daily operations.

Johnathan Hale: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our mergers and acquisitions activity, which has been a key pillar of our inorganic growth strategy this quarter.

In the asset management industry, where organic net flows can be lumpy amid volatile markets, we've leaned into disciplined M&A to accelerate scale, diversify capabilities, and capture pockets of alpha in high-conviction areas like alternatives and ESG-aligned strategies.

The headline deal: the close of our $1.2 billion acquisition of Horizon Alternatives Partners, a New York-based boutique manager specializing in private credit and infrastructure debt, with $18 billion in AUM as of quarter-end. This transaction was immediately accretive to our EPS by approximately 8% on a pro forma basis, driven by Horizon's sticky 45 bps management fee and a low-teens fee-related earnings margin. Post-close, we've already realized $45 million in annualized cost synergies through overlapping functions and system migrations onto our platform.

Strategically, this bolt-on fits our ambition to double alternatives AUM to $150 billion by 2026. Horizon brings differentiated expertise in middle-market direct lending—yields averaging LIBOR + 650 bps net—and a track record of 12% annualized IRRs. We've cross-sold their strategies, securing $2.5 billion in new mandates, with client retention at 98%.

In Europe, we completed a tuck-in acquisition of Verdant Analytics for €250 million, adding €4 billion in AUM focused on SFDR-compliant strategies. This ramps our European AUM to 22% of total.

Our pipeline includes advanced talks for a minority stake in a Singapore-based family office platform with $12 billion in APAC private markets exposure, targeting 25% APAC AUM by 2027.

M&A remains robust, with 45 deals YTD. Valuations at 12-15x fee-related earnings. Our $5 billion dry powder, bolstered by strong free cash flow.

These transactions have driven 12% inorganic AUM growth this quarter, adding 200-250 bps to revenue growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind the acceleration in net flows this quarter?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, Mike. Thanks for the question. As David outlined, fund performance was the cornerstone, driving 45% of our $18.7 billion inflows. Our Alpha Equity Fund delivered top-decile alpha, pulling in $4.8 billion, while fixed income and alts added meaningfully amid rate cuts and yield-seeking. Market trends like the S&P rally and ESG tailwinds amplified this, with ETFs capturing $6.5 billion. Our tech initiatives, including the Advisor Portal, rounded it out. This virtuous cycle positions us for continued momentum.

Mike Johnson: Thank you. And a follow-up on the fee rate stability—how sustainable is the 48 bps blended rate given ETF growth?

Sarah Mitchell: Great question, Mike. We've stabilized at 48 bps through a deliberate mix shift—ETFs at low single digits but scale driving volume, offset by higher-margin alts at 65 bps. Tech overlays like tax-alpha add 5-10 bps embedded value, and we're targeting 50 bps via watermark resets and APAC expansion. Industry compression is real, but our diversification keeps us resilient.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Horizon Growth Equity Fund?

David Kwon: Good morning, Emily. The fund returned 11.5% net in Q3, outpacing the Russell 1000 Growth by 120 bps. Key was our overweight in AI semis and healthcare defensives, capturing 110% of the benchmark amid the Magnificent Seven surge. Risk-adjusted, Sharpe at 1.6, and it's attracted $3.5 billion in active equity flows despite passive trends.

Emily Carter: And how is the new product, the AI Growth ETF, performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Chen: Exceeding expectations, Emily. We've hit $500 million AUM already, with $850 million across active ETF launches. Inflows driven by thematic appeal—AI and renewables—and competitive 25 bps TER. Retail platforms like Schwab are key distribution partners, and we're seeing cross-sell into institutional sleeves.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Michael Torres: Thanks, Raj. Our tech investments, like the Horizon Alpha platform, have cut execution costs to sub-10 bps and boosted flow attribution by 30%. Client portal adoption at 85% reduced churn 15%, enabling $28.4 billion NNA. Synergies from M&A add another layer—$45 million annualized from the Horizon Alternatives deal. Margins expanding toward 45% by 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays.

Laura Kim: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Elena Vasquez: Good question, Laura. Regulations like SFDR, MiFID II, and SEC climate rules are tailwinds—42% of new flows into compliant products, enhancing retention to 96.2%. We've enhanced monitoring of liquidity and volatility risks via AI stress tests, hedging FX on 20% of non-USD AUM. Election volatility is on our radar, but our 55/30/15 allocation is stress-tested to 10% drawdowns. Risk framework keeps us agile.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Horizon Capital Partners. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
